observations: The gate is a plain AND of two flags: eof_ at +0x48 is tested first (jne drain), then read_error_ at +0x49 (je read). Either flag alone takes the drain path; there is no other condition.

end_of_buffer_offset_ advances before the status check: the add at 0x5f019b7-0x5f019bb runs before the cmpb $0,0x10(%rsp) at 0x5f019bf, so a failed read still advances the offset by the partially-read bytes -- matching upstream log_reader.cc:754-756.
buffer_.clear() runs twice on the error path (once before the read, once after the failure) and the stale block is gone before the fresh read, so a failed read can never leave the old block behind.
The eof boundary is exact: cmp $0x7fff,%rax; ja skips the arm, so size 0x7fff sets eof_ and eof_offset_, while a full 0x8000-byte read does not -- matching upstream `buffer_.size() < kBlockSize`.

kBadHeader (12) is written only on the drain path with a non-empty buffer; the empty drain writes kEof (10) with no drop_size write. This is the only place *error = 12 is written, which is why ReadPhysicalRecord can return kBadHeader only through ReadMore.
read_error_ sticks: once set on the error arm, the gate never re-enters the read path, so a WAL read error is terminal for the reader.

The local Status is destroyed on both read-path exits: its state_ pointer (rsp+0x08) is delete[]'d when non-null (0x5f019db-0x5f019e4). The exception landing pad at 0x5f0189a does the same free before resuming unwinding.

One call site, two paths: ReadPhysicalRecord calls ReadMore from a single loop-head site (0x5f01aab); the short-buffer and recyclable-short-header arms both continue back to it. The census (whole-.text E8/E9/LEA scan, Capstone-validated, cross-checked by a second raw scan) finds exactly 1 call, 0 jumps, 0 LEA refs.
